message: Thanks. To check your options in Kentucky, I need three more details: (1) How many people live in your household, including you? (2) How many children under 18 live with you? (3) Does anyone in the household get health insurance through a job?
reply: Three of us. I have my son. Yeah.

message: Thanks. Two quick follow-ups: (1) How old is your son? Is he under 17? (2) Does the job health plan cover your family, and do you pay less than about 10% of your income for the cheapest single-person coverage on it?

Sorry, I didn't catch that. Please give two answers: (1) Your son's age in years (for example, 12). (2) Is the job health plan affordable for you, meaning your share of the cheapest single-person premium is under about 10% of your pay? Answer yes, no, or not sure.

summary: Household: Kentucky, 3 people, one child (son, age not confirmed), household earned income $79,300/yr, owns home, someone has job-based health insurance. Recommended: Child Tax Credit (refundable part), only if the son is under 17; apply through the tax return. Not recommended: SNAP, WIC, TANF, SSI, Medicaid, CHIP, and free/reduced school meals (income is well above the limits for a 3-person household). EITC is out at this income. ACA premium tax credit is unlikely because job coverage is offered; caseworker should confirm whether that employer plan is affordable (under about 10% of pay for the employee-only premium). Hand off to caseworker to verify the son's age and the employer plan's affordability, since the person did not answer those questions.
